spec.full_target: For every nonnegative integer n and every nonempty compact E⊆ℝ^n, with I=[0,1] and E×I given the concatenated Euclidean metric, prove dim_H(E×I)=dim_H(E)+1.

calculations: Concatenated Euclidean distance has squared value |x−y|²+|t−u|²; projections are 1-Lipschitz, and diam(U×J)≤√(diam(U)²+diam(J)²). Subdivide [0,1] into at most 1/r+1 intervals of length at most r for 0<r≤1.

primitives.meaning: The n-dimensional Euclidean space, with ℝ^0 a singleton.
Critical exponent of Hausdorff measures; dim_H(∅)=0.

propositions.statement: If d<dim_H(A), the d-dimensional Hausdorff measure of A is infinite.

source.statement: If d<dim_H(A), the d-dimensional Hausdorff measure of A is infinite.
hypotheses: A is in an extended metric space with its Borel measurable structure; d is NNReal.

propositions.statement: For a countable family of nonnegative measurable ENNReal functions, the integral of the pointwise sum equals the sum of integrals.

source.statement: For a countable family of nonnegative measurable ENNReal functions, the integral of the pointwise sum equals the sum of integrals.
hypotheses: Measurable space with measure; countable index type; all summands AEMeasurable.

argument.text: Set D=dim_H(E), F=E×I. Boundedness from compactness and elementary cube covers of a bounded box show D≤n. For q>D, M001 gives H^q(E)=0. At scale δ≤1 use covers by positive-diameter r_j≤δ with arbitrarily small Σr_j^q; replace singleton members by tiny balls with summable arbitrarily small added cost. Cover I for each j with at most 1/r_j+1 intervals of length ≤r_j. The products cover F, have diameter ≤√2r_j, and total (q+1)-cost ≤2(√2)^(q+1)Σr_j^q. Letting costs and scales tend to zero yields H^(q+1)(F)=0, hence dim_H(F)≤D+1.

If D>0 fix 0<s<D. M001 gives H^s(E)=∞, so scale contents c_s(E,δ) tend to infinity by their defining limit. For an arbitrary cover V_i of F with ρ_i=diam(V_i)≤δ≤1, let A_i,B_i be projections. Enlarge each B_i to an open interval J_i of length ≤ρ_i+η_i, choosing η_i>0 with Ση_iρ_i^s<ε. For every t∈I, the A_i with t∈J_i cover E: each (x,t) belongs to some V_i and B_i⊆J_i. Hence c_s(E,δ)≤Σ1_{J_i}(t)ρ_i^s pointwise. These are nonnegative measurable functions; M002 gives integral of the sum equals the sum of integrals. Integrating over I gives c_s(E,δ)≤Σ(ρ_i+η_i)ρ_i^s≤Σρ_i^(s+1)+ε. Zero-diameter terms vanish since s>0. Let ε→0 and infimize over product covers to obtain c_s(E,δ)≤c_(s+1)(F,δ); hence H^(s+1)(F)=∞ and dim_H(F)≥s+1. Taking every 0<s<D gives dim_H(F)≥D+1.

If D=0 choose x₀∈E by H001. The coordinate projection F→I is onto and 1-Lipschitz by the concatenated Euclidean metric. Directly, every countable cover of I has sum of diameters at least 1 (enlarge each covering set to an interval by arbitrarily small errors), so H^1(I)>0 and dim_H(I)≥1. Interval subdivisions show H^q(I)=0 for q>1, giving dim_H(I)≤1. The Lipschitz-cover estimate dim_H(image)≤dim_H(domain) follows by mapping each covering set and using diameter nonincrease. Thus dim_H(F)≥1=D+1. This holds for n=0 too. Combine with upper bound.

hypothesis_checks: Apply in Euclidean Borel space to E and q>D.
Apply in Euclidean Borel space to E and 0<s<D.
Use counting measure on I and f_i(t)=ρ_i^s·1_{J_i∩I}(t), measurable since J_i is open.
